answer: The missing property was an idempotent write: applying the same rows twice must leave one copy. A plain INSERT cannot tell a retry from new data. The job wrote its rows, then crashed before the success marker, so the retry appended the slice again and doubled the totals. Two safe designs: (1) partition replace, where DELETE of the day's slice and INSERT run in one transaction, so a rerun swaps in a fresh copy of the slice; (2) MERGE keyed on the row key, with a version guard (update only when source version is greater than target version) and tombstones for deletes, so a rerun matches existing rows instead of adding duplicates.
